title: List the sensors we have readings for

spec.plan: Today there is no way to discover which sensors exist: a caller has to already know a sensor name before GET /sensors/{sensor}/summary is useful, and nothing lists them. After this change GET /sensors returns 200 and a JSON array with one object per sensor that has at least one reading - {"sensor": str, "count": int, "latest_reading_at": datetime} - ordered by sensor name ascending, and an empty array when the readings table holds no rows. Two decisions the builder should not re-open: (1) the aggregation is a single SQL GROUP BY in the handler, not a pure helper in app/summary.py, because the repo's "keep arithmetic away from the session" rule is about arithmetic that can be done on values already in hand - grouping in Python would mean loading the whole table, and there is no arithmetic here beyond COUNT and MAX; (2) an empty table is 200 with [], not 404, because "an empty result is not zero" is about refusing to invent a neutral value for one named sensor, and an empty list of sensors is the true answer rather than an invented one. Nothing else changes: app/models.py, app/db.py, app/settings.py and app/summary.py are untouched, no new table, no migration, no new dependency. The existing /sensors/{sensor}/summary route keeps working - the two paths differ in segment count and do not shadow each other (verified).
acceptance_checks: With the sandbox seed applied (kitchen x3, garage x2) and no other rows, `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/sensors` returns HTTP 200 and a JSON array of exactly two objects, the first with "sensor":"garage" and the second with "sensor":"kitchen" - ascending by sensor name.
In that same response the kitchen object has "count": 3 and the garage object has "count": 2 - one entry per sensor, counting its readings, not one entry per reading.

POST a reading for a sensor name that has never been used (`curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/readings -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"sensor":"attic","celsius":4.0}'`), then GET /sensors: an object with "sensor":"attic" and "count":1 is now present, and its "latest_reading_at" is byte-for-byte the "recorded_at" value the POST returned.

POST a second reading for that same sensor, then GET /sensors again: the attic object's "count" is 2 and its "latest_reading_at" has advanced to the second POST's "recorded_at" - the field is the latest reading's time, not the first.
A sensor name that has never been posted does not appear: in the GET /sensors response from the previous check, no object has "sensor":"no-such-sensor".

With the table emptied (`DELETE FROM readings` against DATABASE_URL), `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/sensors` prints 200 and the body is `[]` - not a 404 and not an error.
GET /sensors/kitchen/summary still returns 200 with count 3, and GET /sensors/nope/summary still returns 404 - adding /sensors did not shadow the existing summary route.
tests_added: tests/test_api.py::test_sensors_lists_each_sensor_once_with_its_reading_count - POST two readings under sensor "test-sensors-a" and one under "test-sensors-b", GET /sensors, and assert the entry for each has the expected count. Assert by looking the sensor up in the response, never by asserting the length of the whole list: the suite and the sandbox seed both leave other sensors in the table.
tests/test_api.py::test_sensors_are_ordered_by_name - GET /sensors and assert the list of "sensor" values equals its own sorted() copy. Self-contained whatever else is in the table.

tests/test_api.py::test_sensors_reports_the_time_of_the_most_recent_reading - POST two readings under "test-sensors-latest", keep both "recorded_at" values from the responses, and assert that entry's "latest_reading_at" equals the second one and not the first.
tests/test_api.py::test_a_sensor_that_never_reported_is_absent_from_the_list - GET /sensors and assert no entry has sensor "test-sensors-never", a name nothing posts.

research.claim: The request is exactly: list every sensor with at least one reading, with its reading count and its latest reading's time, ordered by sensor name. Field set and ordering come from that sentence; nothing beyond it is in scope.
research.source: https://github.com/bsf-fixtures/py-api/issues/9 - the issue body, read in full.

research.claim: `/sensors` is the right path and does not shadow the existing `/sensors/{sensor}/summary` route; declaration order does not matter.
research.source: ran: prototyped both routes in a scratch copy and read GET /openapi.json - paths were ['/health', '/readings', '/sensors', '/sensors/{sensor}/summary'], and GET /sensors/kitchen/summary still returned 200 while GET /sensors/nope/summary still returned 404. Existing route at app/main.py:63.

research.claim: The response model is `SensorOut(sensor: str, count: int, latest_reading_at: datetime)` in app/schemas.py. `count` matches the name SensorSummary already uses for a row count; `latest_reading_at` is named after the `recorded_at` column it is the MAX of.

The handler pattern to follow: build the statement, `with session() as db:`, then construct the pydantic model explicitly from the columns rather than handing back ORM rows. app/db.py's session() is the only way to get a Session and the new handler uses it.

Reading the aggregates off the Row by name does NOT type-check: `.label('count')` plus `row.count` fails mypy strict with `List comprehension has incompatible type List[tuple[Any, Callable[[Any], int], Any]]`, because Row subclasses tuple and `.count` resolves to `tuple.count`. Unpack the row instead - `for sensor, count, latest in db.execute(stmt).all()` - which is clean. No `# type: ignore`; there is none anywhere in this repo.
research.source: ran: `.venv/bin/mypy --strict` on both forms against this repo's app package, mypy 2.4.1 with strict = true; then `.venv/bin/mypy app` and `.venv/bin/ruff check .` (ruff 0.17.6) on the full prototype - both clean.

research.claim: `select(Reading.sensor, func.count(Reading.id), func.max(Reading.recorded_at)).group_by(Reading.sensor).order_by(Reading.sensor)` returns exactly what is needed, in ascending name order, with count already a Python int and the max already a tz-aware datetime - no post-processing. Against an empty table it returns [], which is where the 200-with-[] behaviour comes from rather than from a guess.
research.source: ran: that statement against a real PostgreSQL on 127.0.0.1:5432 with rows for kitchen x2, garage x1, attic x1 - got [('attic', 1, datetime), ('garage', 1, datetime), ('kitchen', 2, datetime)]; then `DELETE FROM readings` and re-ran it - got [].

research.claim: latest_reading_at serializes in the same ISO-8601 UTC form as ReadingOut.recorded_at, so acceptance check 3 can compare the two strings directly.
research.source: ran: the prototype through fastapi.testclient - GET /sensors returned 200 and [{"sensor":"attic","count":2,"latest_reading_at":"2026-11-21T06:56:33.470833Z"}, ...], matching the recorded_at the POST had returned.

research.claim: The new handler's lines are uncovered without new tests, so the four tests listed are what carries the diff past the 80% diff-coverage floor. The existing 18 tests all pass unchanged with the endpoint added.
research.source: ran: `.venv/bin/pytest -q --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing` on the prototype with no new tests - 18 passed, 93% total, new handler lines listed under Missing for app/main.py. Floor is .factory/guardrails/coverage.json#diff_min_pct = 80.

research.claim: The sandbox can exercise every acceptance check here: the seed gives kitchen x3 and garage x2 (the expected counts in checks 1 and 2), and a fifth read-only HTTP endpoint is the same class of thing the manifest already claims to exercise. Nothing in capabilities.not_exercised is touched, since app/models.py and app/db.py are not in `files`.

New tests must name their sensors `test-sensors-*` and must assert by looking an entry up, never by asserting the length of the whole list. The suite leaves its rows behind and the sandbox's test command deletes only `sensor LIKE 'test-%'`; the seeded kitchen and garage rows remain, so `len(body) == 2` would pass once and fail on a seeded or re-run database.
research.source: .factory/definition/context/history.md - the first two lessons; .factory/sandbox/manifest.json#commands.test, whose preamble is the DELETE.

research.claim: The two house rules this change could be read as breaking - "An empty result is not zero" and "Keep arithmetic away from the session" - are not broken by it, for the reasons given in `plan`. The four test names are written in the repo's "a test name states its claim" register.

research.claim: list_sensors needs `.all()` on the Result, not `.scalars().all()`: scalars() collapses to the first column, which is what the other two read handlers want and this one does not.
research.source: https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/21/orm/queryguide/select.html - "Selecting ORM Entities and Attributes" / Result rows; SQLAlchemy 2.1.9 is what installs here, pyproject.toml pins `sqlalchemy>=2.0`.
